sentences.text: However, the appeal is filed after a delay of 206 days beyond the statutory limitation period of 120 days prescribed under Section 74(1) of the Act.
This Court, following the Division Bench ruling in MFA NC: 2024:KHC-K:10194 No.102543/2022 dated 23.09.2024, holds that the limitation period under the Act is mandatory and non- extendable.

Relying on precedents,
including Union of India vs. Popular Construction Co. and State of Kerala vs. V.R. Kalliyanikutty reported in AIR 1999 SC 1305, the appeal is dismissed as time-barred, without addressing the merits.

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum
 Oral Judgment
(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)
The present appeal, filed under Section 74(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, challenges the judgment and award dated 12.04.2022 in LAC No.235/2018.
However, the appeal is filed after a delay of 206 days beyond the statutory limitation period of 120 days prescribed under Section 74(1) of the Act.
This Court, following the Division Bench ruling in MFA NC: 2024:KHC-K:10194 No.102543/2022 dated 23.09.2024, holds that the limitation period under the Act is mandatory and non- extendable.
